title: Théorie des cycles algébriques : conjectures de Hodge, Tate, Lefschetz, Weil : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (pp. 67-69). X and Y are smooth projective varieties, with n = dim X. Grothendieck writes A_X for the Albanese variety of X, since he uses H^1(A_X,Q_l) ≅ H^1(X,Q_l). He writes B_X for the Picard variety Pic^0(X), since H^1(B_X,Q_l) ≅ H^{2n-1}(X,Q_l)(n-1). A_k and A^k denote cycle groups of dimension and codimension k.

Two kinds of correspondence:
- A divisor D ∈ A^1(X×Y) gives a homomorphism u_D : A_Y → B_X (Alb Y → Pic^0 X). Its cohomological shadow is a(γ(D)) : H^{2n-1}(X)(n-1) → H^1(Y).
- A 1-cycle Z ∈ A_1(X×Y)⊗Q goes the other way. It gives a quasi-homomorphism u_Z : B_X → A_Y (pull a degree-0 divisor back to Z, push to Y via Albanese). Its shadow is a(γ(Z)) : H^1(Y) → H^{2n-1}(X)(n-1). This is construction '2.1'.

Proposition 2.7 (end of p. 67, finished here). a(γ(D)) is an isomorphism iff u_D is an isogeny. In that case there is a Q-1-cycle Z, independent of l, whose cohomology class inverts a(γ(D)). Moreover u_Z is the quasi-isogeny u_D^{-1}.

Proof on this page. There is a commutative square: Ψ_X : H^{2n-1}(X)(n-1) ≅ H^1(B_X) and Φ_Y : H^1(A_Y) ≅ H^1(Y), with u_D^{(1)} : H^1(B_X) → H^1(A_Y) along the bottom. So a(γ(D)) is an isomorphism iff u_D^*(1) is, iff u_D is an isogeny, since H^1 of an abelian variety detects isogenies.

For existence of Z: the inverse quasi-isogeny u_D^{-1} is 'algebraic' in Hom⊗Q. So one only needs Φ_Y^{-1} and Ψ_X^{-1} to be induced by Q-algebraic cycles, uniformly in l. For Ψ_X this is the special case of 2.7 for the canonical map defined by the Poincaré divisorial correspondence D ∈ Cl(X,B_X). One must find a canonical 1-cycle Z ∈ A_1(X×B_X) inverting it.

The next page does this. Choose a polarization ξ. Use the square formed by hard Lefschetz cup ξ^{n-1} : H^1(X) → H^{2n-1}(X)(n-1), φ_X, ψ_X, and μ : H^1(A_X) → H^1(B_X). Here μ comes from the polarization isogeny between Albanese and Picard, which can be inverted as a Q-isogeny. So everything is algebraic.

Purpose. This is the degree-1 case of the Lefschetz standard conjecture B and of the algebraicity of inverses of correspondences. It is proved by reducing everything to Picard/Albanese theory, independent of l and valid in any characteristic.
errors: The page has a notational trap rather than an error: A_X is the Albanese and B_X the Picard variety, the reverse of many modern conventions. The previous page's u_D : A_Y → B_X is consistent with this page's diagram.

In the Ψ_X reduction, 'prouver 2.7 dans le cas particulier' looks circular, but it is only a reduction to the universal (Poincaré) case. That case is then settled independently on the next page via the polarization isogeny. No gap.

Hard Lefschetz in degree 1 (cup ξ^{n-1}, l-adic, arbitrary characteristic) is used implicitly on the next page. It is legitimate in degree 1 because it follows from the polarization isogeny Alb → Pic^0 (Weil). The page does not say this explicitly.

ideas.what: Divisorial correspondences D on X×Y give Alb(Y)→Pic^0(X), and Q-1-cycles give Pic^0(X)→Alb(Y). Their l-adic classes in H^{2n-1}(X)(n-1)↔H^1(Y) are compatible with H^1 of the abelian varieties.
ideas.modern_name: Correspondences acting on Picard/Albanese; motives h^1 and h^{2n-1} as motives of abelian varieties (Murre's Picard and Albanese motives)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Weil (correspondences/abelian varieties), Grothendieck; Murre (1990) for the motivic decomposition
ideas.where_published: Spirit appears in 'Standard conjectures on algebraic cycles' (1969); details in Kleiman, 'Algebraic cycles and the Weil conjectures' (Dix exposés, 1968)

ideas.what: If a divisorial correspondence induces an isomorphism H^{2n-1}(X)(n-1) → H^1(Y), its inverse is induced by an algebraic Q-1-cycle independent of l. The proof goes through quasi-isogenies and the polarization isogeny.
ideas.modern_name: Lefschetz standard conjecture B (and inverse-algebraicity) in degree 1
ideas.usually_credited_to: Lieberman (1968), Kleiman (1968), attributing the method to Grothendieck
ideas.where_published: Standard conjectures on algebraic cycles (Bombay 1968, publ. 1969): conjecture known in degree ≤1 via Picard/Albanese

ideas.what: Isogeny is detected by an isomorphism on H^1; Q-isogenies are invertible in Hom⊗Q.
ideas.modern_name: Basic theory of abelian varieties up to isogeny

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful draft of the well-known degree-1 case of the Lefschetz/standard conjectures via Picard and Albanese varieties. It was published shortly afterwards by Kleiman and Lieberman and mentioned by Grothendieck himself. Nothing appears new beyond seeing the proof in his hand around 1965.
transcription_corrections: Beginning of the 'Pour Ψ_X' sentence: more plausibly 'Pour Ψ_X, on est donc ramené à prouver 2.7 dans le cas particulier de l'hom. can.' rather than 'c'est donc venu : prouver 2.7'.
Crossed-out heading: possibly 'Théorème / On écrit le diagramme ...'; it is struck through and immaterial.
'(quasi isog.)' after u_Z is correct: u_Z is a quasi-isogeny (isogeny tensor Q).
Diagram target: H^1(A_Y,Q_l) with Φ_Y going up to H^1(Y,Q_l), as transcribed. The right-hand label of the left arrow is a struck-out '≀' and annotation.
